title: [finding] engine.ts ADR-0061 docblock still describes search expansion as `$or` of `$contains` — the implementation and its own neighbor file say `$icontains`
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` seat on behalf of the flight-③ sweep dev (its repo-scoped REST was 403, so it reported the finding on #13717 instead of opening it blind; this seat re-verified the premise and dedup-searched with a non-empty control before filing).

## Measured, at origin/main this hour

- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:8550` — the ADR-0061 docblock (near the search-expansion helper shared by `find` and `findOne`) describes the expansion as "a server-resolved cross-field `$or` of `$contains`".
- `packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts:8-30` — the implementation one file over emits `$or` of **`$icontains`**, and its own header documents the correction explicitly: "[#7641] The case-insensitive operator is `$icontains`, NOT `$contains`."

## Why it is worth a card at all

Comment-only, zero behavior — severity low. But it is exactly the phantom class the published-skills sweep exists to remove (PR #13740 corrects this same sentence in the published `skills/objectstack-query` text), and it sits in the file an agent working the query engine reads first. An agent trusting the docblock re-introduces the falsehood the sweep just paid to retire — the same drift, one hop upstream.

Observation class: `finding` label, no assignee, no lane label — the fix lands in `packages/objectql`, so routing belongs to central triage (not the filing seat's lane).

Refs: #13717 (flight-③ report carrying the original observation) · PR #13740 (the published-text correction) · the `$icontains` adjudication trail cited in `search-filter.ts` (#7641 / #6520 / #6682).
